title: Critical season ahead for Virginia Tech football program | Special Sections | timesnews.net
text:
The Virginia Tech football program took a step back in 2024, a season when they were expected to leap forward. Now comes a critical 2025 campaign for the Hokies in their fourth season under head coach Brent Pry.
Expectations were high for Virginia Tech last season with 21 starters back. Unfortunately for the Hokies, they were upset by Vanderbilt in week 1 and never fully got on track with a 6-6 season.
Pry insists the roster is deeper this season and the team has improved its strength and conditioning.
“We made some upticks in very important areas in our program,” Pry said. “We’ve had an influx of talented transfers, high school signees and young men we’ve developed in the program. We reflected on the 2024 year and we have to be a more mentally and physically tough team.”
They open the season with another SEC team, South Carolina at a neutral-site game in Atlanta. The Gamecocks are led by Shane Beamer, the son of legendary Virginia Tech coach Frank Beamer. Pry talked about the excitement surrounding the game.
“The opportunity to play on the big stage, to play on national TV, that is why these young men come to Virginia Tech,” Pry said. “We play a marquee team that’s very talented, well coached and arguably a playoff team last year. We’ve got a lot to prove in Blacksburg.”
Virginia Tech will have a chance to avenge last year’s loss to Vanderbilt in a home game in week 2. The first four games are non-conference before heading to N.C. State for the first ACC contest on Sept. 27.
Kyron Drones, a redshirt senior, is back at quarterback after having his season cut short by injury last season. He completed 61 percent of his passes for 1,562 yards and 10 touchdowns in nine games as starter before missing the other four. He played in all 13 games the previous season and was starter in 11 of them.
Pop Watson, who filled in when Drones was injured, returns as well. He completed 14 of 21 passes for 254 yards and rushed for another 48 yards to lead the Hokies to a 37-17 win over rival Virginia. Garrett Rangel, a transfer from Oklahoma State, is also competing for playing time.
The biggest hole to fill is running back where the Hokies look to replace Bhayshul Tuten who rushed for 1,159 yards last season and averaged 6.3 yards per carry. Bowling Green transfer Terion Stewart (5-9, 220) is a powerful back who rushed for 898 yards for the Falcons last season.
Returners Jeremiah Coney and P.J. Prioleau, who suffered injuries last season, should give Tech some depth at the position.
Donovan Greene, a Wake Forest transfer, could make a major impact at wide receiver after being healed from a knee injury. Cameron Seldon, who played running back at Tennessee, is being projected as a wide receiver. Among the returning players, Ayden Greene, a Powell High School alum, is looking for a breakout season.
Redshirt junior tight end Benji Gosnell should be another big target. He caught 32 passes last season, while Harrison Saint Germain is also used heavily, but more as a blocking tight end.
The entire starting offensive line from last season is gone.
Kyle Altuner, a redshirt freshman at 6-3, 296 pounds, impressed the coaches in the spring. The high school All-American is projected to be the starting center. Tomas Rimas, a redshirt senior transfer from West Virginia, was an All-Big 12 selection at guard last season.
Montavius Cunningham, a redshirt senior from Georgia State, could be a standout at tackle. Johnny Garrett, a redshirt junior transfer from Boston College, and Layth Ghannam, a transfer from George Washington, could also find plenty of playing time. The obvious question is how the line will mesh with all new pieces.
Jaden Keller, the former Tennessee High star, is expected to be a leader on the defensive side of the ball. The senior linebacker played in all 13 games last season and started seven. He had a team-high 83 tackles last season as well as two fumble recoveries.
Caleb Woodson, second on the team with 72 tackles last season, returns for his junior season. Other linebackers expected to make an impact are Kaleb Spencer and Pittsburgh transfer Jordan Bass, lean and fast at 6-3 and 205 pounds.
James Djonkam is a huge addition to the defensive line. The graduate transfer led Eastern Michigan with 98 tackles last season. Kevin Gilliam Jr. is another force up front. He made 35 tackles for the Hokies a year ago.
Kemari Copeland is eager to get back to form after coming back from an injury. Ben Bell should be another impactful transfer coming from Texas State.
Brothers Quentin Reddish and Joseph Reddick will be part of the last line of defense in the backfield. Dante Lovett is a capable cornerback, while Isaiah Cash is a big pickup from Sam Houston State after 67 tackles last season.
Other transfers include Isaiah Brown-Murray, who had 30 solo tackles for East Carolina, and Sherrod Covil from Clemson.
John Love gives the Hokies great range at kicker. He hit a 60-yard field goal against Minnesota in last season’s Duke’s Mayo Bowl.
There are a lot of new pieces with the question of how will they mesh during the upcoming season.
